 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident. 
2. The case of the petitioner is as follows: That on 29082022 at about 915 p.m., when petitioner was crossing the road on Hesaraghatta main road and proceeding towards Bank of India,
at that time all of a sudden a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA04KJ4266 riding by its rider at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came on wrong lane from 8th Maile towards Bagalagunte and lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the petitioner's, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his left leg, right leg and injuries to other parts body. 
Immediately he was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient, he is still bed ridden and under treatment, he has spent Rs.2, 50,000/ towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses, he has to incur future medical expenses. He was working as a Helper and earning Rs.25, 000/ per month. Due to permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work. He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and nonpecuniary damages. 
3. Respondent No.1 -HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co.Ltd.,/ Insurer of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04KJ4266 has filed written statement denying the petition averments. They have admitted the coverage of policy in respect of offending vehicle and stated that petitioner in collision with jurisdictional police have created false records and story about the manner and involvement of motorcycle to get compensation and lodged a false complaint and that accident in question has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner who was crossing the road without having proper look on vehicular movements on the road and there is no zebra crossing. 
4. The respondent no.2 Harish Kumar/R.C owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA04KJ 4266 has contended that the compensation amount claimed by the petitioner is excessive,
exorbitant, unreasonable and speculative in nature and that offending vehicle is insured with respondent no1 and all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force . 
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 29082022 at about 915 p.m., near Bank of India,
Hesaraghatta main road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA04kJ4266?
Vishnu.R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/
2 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount, if so what is the quantum? From whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
6. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P21 and closed his side. The respondents have not adduced rebuttal evidence.
7. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and the respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record. 
8. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following; 
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 :  In order to prove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 29082022 at about 915 p.m. when he was crossing the road on Hesaraghatta main road at that time the rider of the offending vehicle by riding it in rash and negligent manner hit against him. The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
10. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 which are the police records such as F.I.R., statement, crime details form along with spot mahazar, spot sketch, 133 notice, 133 reply notice, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.
11. The respondent no.1 and 2 have disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioner and submitted that rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner alone is the cause for accident, as the petitioner without observing the vehicular movement in the road all of a sudden crossed the road and came in contact with the offending vehicle. 
12. Now in order to prove the issue no.1, it is better to have glance on the evidence of PW.1,
complaint, the spot mahazar and sketch. The PW.1 in his cross examination has deposed that at the time of accident he was crossing the road, that there was heavy traffic in the said road, that there was centre median between the two roads, that there was no zebra crossing at the place where he has crossed the road and that prior to the accident he has not witnessed the motorcycle coming in the said road. In the complaint also the complainant has stated that at the time when the petitioner was crossing the road he met with an accident and sustained injuries. 
Vishnu.R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/
3 13. If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 60 feet; there is divider between the two roads of the width of 30 feet each. The petitioner while crossing the road met with an accident. The spot of accident is somewhere in the middle of the road. 
As admitted by PW.1 there was no zebra crossing at the spot of accident. The PW.1 being the pedestrian while crossing the road ought to have taken all caution to see whether any vehicles are coming in both direction of the road and it is only after confirming that no vehicles are coming in near distance, he had to step in to the road. At the same time when the said road is a straight road and sufficiently wide road , the rider of the motorcycle if he was vigilant and if he had ridden his vehicle in moderate speed, on seeing the person crossing the road he could have applied break and he could have avoided the accident. 
14. Learned counsel for the respondent no.1 at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in ILR 1998 Kar 1934 between Narasimhaish Vs., The General Manager & Anr., In the said case, the pedestrian had crossed the road at a point where he ought not to have crossed the road. The Hon'ble High Court by observing that petitioner too has contributed negligence has fixed ratio of 40 as negligence contributed by the petitioner. 
15. In ILR 1987 Karnataka page 2730 between Sharada Bai Vs. KSRTC., it is held that :
"A driver, particularly of a publictransport vehicle, is expected to have a proper look out and provide for the safety of the other users of the road. In a busy city, a driver must anticipated and provided for the more common follies of other users of the road. In crowded city roads it is not un often that pedestrians dart across the road,
cyclist and scooterists attempt to weave a zig zag path between other moving vehicles; school children who are left to fend for themselves, cross the streets unmindful of the hazards of traffic; and all these are a part of the realities of the urban predicament, which any driver, more particularly of a public transport system,
ought to be cognizant of. He must keep his anticipatory reflexes geared to be able to stop the vehicle at a very shortnotice. Roads are not meant only for heavyvehicles;
they are also meant for other users of the road and the drivers of heavy vehicles must negotiate their vehicles in such a way as not to jeopardise the safety of the other users of the road". 
"If the tortfeasor's negligence or breach of duty is established as causative of the damage, the onus is on him to establish that the victim's contributory negligence was a substantial or cooperating cause. In order to establish the defence of contributory negligence the propounder of that defence must prove, first, that the victim failed to take reasonable care of himself or, in other words, such care as a man of ordinary prudence would have done and that was a contributory cause of the accident. The amount of care which a person could reasonably be expected to take,
must needs vary with the circumstances and conditions actually prevailing at the material point of time. However, it is relevant to note that, in order to discharge of burden of proof, it is unnecessary for the propounder of that defence to adduce evidence about the matter. Contributory negligence can be and very often is Vishnu.R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/
4 inferred from the evidence already adduced on the claimants behalf or from the perceptive facts, either admitted or found established, on a balance of probabilities in the case".
16. In unreported judgment rendered in MFA No. 7070/2015 (MV) between Smt.Mina Limbu &
Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd., it was held by referring the facts of the case that "pedestrian crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have done, it has to be considered that pedestrian too has contributed negligence. In the said case, 25% of negligence was attributed against the deceased. 
17. In MFA NO.2380/2016 between Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr., in the said case also referring some of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it has observed that "where the person is crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing and accident occurs,
some percentage of negligence has to be attributed against the person who crossed the road and met with an accident". In the said case, 20% negligence was attributed against the deceased. 
18. Further in MFA No.2613/2010 Smt.N.Bharathamma & Ors., Vs. Mr.Syed Masood Matheen &
Anr., in the said case also by observing that deceased has contributed 25% to the occurrence and in the said case also the deceased while crossing the road had met with an accident. 
19. Hence, considering the materials placed on record, it can be said that the petitioner too has contributed negligence by crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have crossed the road and thereby contributed negligence to an extent of 20%. Hence, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 20% towards the negligence contributed by him. Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in Partly Affirmative. 
20. Issue No.2: The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustaining grievous injuries. 
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.8 and Ex10. On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 29082022 to 14092022 at Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru for a period of 17 days. As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained five injuries, of which injury no.4 and 5 are grievous in nature. 
21. Dr.Srinivasaiah Medical Record clerk at Sapthagiri Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and produced MLC extract, Inpatient case sheet, xray at Ex.P.16 to 18.
22. Dr.S.A Somashekar Orthopedic surgeon at Bowring & lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, is examined as Pw3. Through him OP card with examination report, recent xray films, old xray films are marked as Ex.P.19 to 21. Pw.3 deposed that he has examined the petitioner clinical and radiologically to assess the disabilities, that the petitioner has permanent disability of all 3 limbs at 71% and that of the whole body at 35%. PW.3 further deposed that petitioner is advised for implant removal surgery at 3 sites which would cost around Rs.50,000/ in private set up. Hence,
considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, and this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads. 
Vishnu. R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/ 
5 23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries in nature. 
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/ towards pain and suffering. 
24. So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, the petitioner has not produced inpatient bill. It is submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that the inpatient bill is not included in the medical expense calculated by them and that inpatient bill is covered under ESI hence only they have not produced the inpatient bill and they have claimed compensation under the medical expenses only in respect of Pharmacy bill. The pharmacy bill produced by the petitioner if calculated it comes around Rs.64,096/. The learned counsel for the petitioner during the course of argument referred about the inpatient bill one annexed in the case sheet. If the said inpatient bill is perused, the final bill was issued for Rs.1,14,636/ and the entire final bill of Rs.1,14,636/ was covered under ESI. If inpatient bill is carefully perused, it includes pharmacy bill produced by the petitioner at serial No.22 to 24, 26 to 29, 31 to 44 amounting to Rs.28,600/. Hence, out of Rs.64,096/ sum of Rs.28,600/ which is included in final bill has to be deducted. On such deduction the medical bill comes around Rs.35,492/. Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under medical expenses to the tune of Rs.35,496/.
25. It is stated that petitioner was 21 years and working as helper and earning Rs.25,000/. But to substantiate the said contention, petitioner has not produced any materials. Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs 15,500/ p.m.
26. The petitioner has sustained three grievous injuries and taken treatment for 17 days as inpatient in Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru. Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period. 
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs 15,500/ p.m. for three months. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.46,500/ towards loss of income during the laid down period . 
27. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times. Further for 17 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment. He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses. Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/ taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022. 
28. P.W.3 deposed that the petitioner has 35% permanent disability on all 3 limbs. 
29. The petitioner contended that he is aged about 21 years as on the date of accident. Petitioner has produced Ex.P11/Aadhar card which shows his date of birth as 12052001 that means he was aged 21 years. Hence considering the Aadhar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 21 Vishnu. R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/
6 years.
30. The learned counsel at this juncture, has referred the judgment rendered in MFA No.4840/2011 (MV) between K Kumar Vs., the Manager, M/s Balaji Allianz Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., & Arn., wherein the doctor has assessed the disability at 27% and whole body disability at 13.5%. It was observed by the Hon'ble High Court that "actually the whole body disability would be 1/3 of functional disability".
31. In the present case, PW.3 stated that petitioner has disability of 71% on three limbs and that of whole body at 35%. Admittedly, the PW.3 has not given treatment to the petitioner. It is admitted by PW.3 that there is no mention in the discharge summary of Sapthgiri Hospital about surgery conducted on the hand of the petitioner but only mentioned about plaster applied to the hand. It is admitted by PW.3 that the fractures of the petitioner are united and that Pw2 has assessed only the physical disability of the petitioner but not functional disability. Hence, considering the observation made in the aforesaid rulings and the evidence of PW.3 this court inclines to take the disability of petitioner at 18%. 
32. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/ p.m and if 18% of loss of earning capacity on whole body is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 21 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'. So by applying the multiplier '18' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.6,02,640/ (i.e., 15,500 x 18% x 18 x12 ). Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,02,640/ towards future loss of income due to disability. 
33. P.W.3 has stated that petitioner has to undergo another surgery for implants removal at 3 sites which would cost around Rs.50,000/. Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under the head future medical expenses. Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl . N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/
 charges and nourishing food 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 46,500/
 laid up period 4. Future Loss of Income Rs.6,02,640/
5. Medical expenses Rs. 35,496/
6. Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/
 Total Rs.8,14,636/ 
Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,14,636/ (Rupees Eight Lakh Fourteen Thousand Six Hundred Thirty Six only). 
34. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st Vishnu.R vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163623399/
7 respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident. Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle. Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident. Since both petitioner and respondent no1 had contributed negligence to the extent of 20:80 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%. The respondent no 1 being the insurer is liable to pay 80% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners. 80% of the compensation shall carry interest at 6 % p.a. 
Accordingly issue no 2 is answered. 
35. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order. 
:: ORDER :: 
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs. 
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation Rs.8,14,636/ (Rupees Eight Lakh Fourteen Thousand Six Hundred Thirty Six only). 
The Respondent No 1 is liable to pay 80% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.6,51,709/ with interest there on at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award. 
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.6,21,709/ from the date of petition till the date of deposit. 
Petitioner shall forgo 20% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.1,62,927/.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. Draw award accordingly. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 7th day of March 2024.) (ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl.
SCJ & ACMM Bengaluru.
